title: I built a complete one-level beat'em up using AI, traditional game dev tools, and my own engine. Here's what I learned.
author: JuaniSixto
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with AI-assisted game development and wanted to see how far I could push a solo workflow.

The result is Fatman Returns, a one-level beat’em up demo built using a combination of AI and traditional game development.

One important detail: the game was built using my own engine and game creation tools, which I’ve been developing over the last few years.

For this project I used AI-assisted workflows for:

* Concept art
* Character design
* Backgrounds
* Voice-over
* Sound effects
* Trailer creation
* Marketing assets

combined with traditional game development, level design and a lot of manual iteration.

A quick note: yes, I’m aware there was already a Fatman point-and-click game released in 2015. I actually love that game. This project is a non-commercial fandom experiment and isn’t affiliated with it in any way.

What surprised me most wasn’t the final result, but how quickly I could move from an idea to a playable prototype.

I’m curious:

For those of you using AI in game development, what parts of your workflow have changed the most over the last year?
